open_questions: Mass remains unknown: 1.22 Rearth on a 0.36 Msun M dwarf can be planetary, but RV/photometry still needed to rule out a brown-dwarf/short-period EB given low xgboost planet_rank 0.11
Transit depth scatter (transit_depths chi2 807.5 dof 424, p_consistent 3.257e-26 and sector p_constant 4.378e-63) should be checked with detrending against spot modulation
Stellar binarity indicators (ruwe 1.199, excess_noise_sig 16.43) are not coincident with the transit but reinforce the need for RV to test for an undetected companion
dossier.public_summary: The 2.28-day dip is centred on the M dwarf, flat-bottomed and ~1.2 Earth radii with no odd-even or deep secondary eclipse, so a planet is the best explanation despite a strong spot signal. The star spins at the same period with ~8000-40000 ppm variability and the transit depth wanders, which can mimic depth changes. A radial-velocity mass measurement is still needed to confirm the planet, but a background or on-target blended binary is ruled out by centroid and neighbours.

reasons.why: difference imaging puts the dip on the target (offset 3.417 arcsec, sigma 2.565) with all plausible neighbours >26 sigma away; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 rules out a blended eclipsing binary in the aperture.
shape is not V-shaped (v_sigma negative) but flat-bottomed with best_ingress_fraction 0.05, consistent with a planetary transit rather than a grazing binary.

radius 1.22 Rearth is planet-sized; odd_even diff_sigma 1.42 shows no odd/even difference and secondary snr 9.865 at phase 0.3187 is 145.6 ppm (0.1648 of dip) with best_brightening_snr 27.76, not a stellar secondary; duration ratio 1.594 is elongated but central for a small M dwarf.

large out-of-transit swing tracks the stellar rotation, not a close binary phase curve: rotation.signal_over_rotation 1.0008619173262971 and amplitudes 9000-42887 ppm in sectors 1-2, etc., show a spotted M dwarf (Teff 3387 K, rad 0.3726 Rsun) whose spin period equals the 2.28 d dip period by chance — rotation counts only with a non-transit shape, which is absent.

depth does vary within SPOC, but stellar variability amplitude ~820 ppm comparable to the 883.5 ppm dip and transit_depths share_of_top_3 0.056 with mean_depth 851 ppm across 425 transits shows the signal is not from a few bad events; depth changes are driven by spot-crossing/ systematics on an active rotator, not an EB, while centroid and flat bottom remain consistent with a planet.
